title: Bib Gourmand vs Michelin Star: What's the Difference?
description: Bib Gourmand vs Michelin star vs the Michelin Guide: what each means, what you’ll pay, and the symbols to look for, explained in one table.
h1: Bib Gourmand vs Michelin Star vs the Michelin Guide
summary: What a star, a Bib Gourmand and a plain Guide listing each mean, and what you’ll pay.
body:
A Michelin star rates the cooking itself, from one to three stars. A Bib Gourmand marks restaurants serving good food at a moderate price. Being in the MICHELIN Guide, with or without either award, means inspectors recommend the restaurant. All three come from the same anonymous inspectors.

The terms get mixed up all the time, especially in places where the Guide is new, such as the Philippines. Here is the difference between a Bib Gourmand vs a Michelin star, and between the Michelin Guide vs a Michelin star, in one table and a few short sections.

Bib Gourmand vs Michelin star vs the Guide, side by side

RecognitionWhat it meansPrice to expectWhat diners see
Michelin star (one to three)Outstanding cooking, judged only on the food. Three stars is the highest rating.Typical dinner tasting menu {{price1}} at one star, {{price2}} at two and {{price3}} at three, per personOne, two or three red star symbols (a rounded, flower-like shape)
Bib GourmandHigh-quality food at great value, usually simpler cookingModerate, under a price limit set for each countryThe face of Bibendum, the Michelin Man, licking his lips
In the MICHELIN GuideRecommended by inspectors for good cooking with quality ingredients, without a star or BibAnything from street food to fine diningA listing in the Guide and its app
Green StarSustainable practices; being phased out from 2026Any levelA green star, alongside any red stars

Definitions from the MICHELIN Guide. Star prices are the median dinner tasting menu, per person before service, across restaurants with published prices on The Starred Bill, in US dollars. Last checked {{checked}}.

The key point is that every Michelin-starred restaurant and every Bib Gourmand is in the Guide, but most restaurants in the Guide hold neither. Michelin calls an unadorned listing “simply a good meal”: in its own words, a sign of quality ingredients that are well cooked. So a restaurant described as “Michelin-recommended” or “in the Michelin Guide” isn’t necessarily starred.

What a Bib Gourmand means

The Bib Gourmand, introduced in 1997, is named after Bibendum, the Michelin Man, and recognizes restaurants that serve high-quality food at great value. The cooking tends to be simpler than at a starred restaurant, the kind of food you might try to recreate at home, but done very well.

Each country sets its own price limit for a Bib meal, adjusted for local prices, but the principle is the same everywhere: a full meal that feels like a bargain for the quality. Prices sit far below a starred tasting menu, which typically costs {{price1}} or more per person, though a few starred restaurants serve a meal for under {{valueUSD}}.

That is why many diners prefer Bib restaurants. They tend to be easier to book, more relaxed, and better suited to a normal weeknight. In cities like Singapore, Bangkok and Manila, Bibs also cover hawker stalls and street-food vendors, and those listings are among the Guide’s most useful pages for visitors.

Can a Bib Gourmand restaurant earn a Michelin star?

Yes. A Bib Gourmand isn’t a lower step on the star ladder: it’s a different kind of recognition. But inspectors reassess every restaurant in the Guide each year, and when a Bib kitchen’s cooking reaches star level, it can be promoted. It then loses the Bib, since a restaurant can’t hold both. Some chefs choose to stay at Bib level on purpose, keeping their prices and their style simple.

Where the Green Star fits

The Green Star recognised sustainable practices and could sit alongside red stars, a Bib or a plain listing. Michelin announced in May 2026 that it is being phased out. See the Green Michelin Star explained.

Michelin Guide vs Michelin star: which should you trust?

Use both, for different meals. The Guide’s full selection is a reliable list of good restaurants at every price. The stars point you to the cooking inspectors rank highest, and to the price that comes with it. If you are deciding whether a starred meal is worth it, compare what dinner, lunch and wine pairings cost on our city pages, such as Metro Manila and Singapore. For the full story behind the stars, start with What is a Michelin star?

faq.q: Is a Bib Gourmand a Michelin star?
faq.a: No. A Bib Gourmand is a separate award for good food at a moderate price. A Michelin star rates the cooking itself, at one, two or three stars. A restaurant can’t hold a star and a Bib at the same time.

faq.q: Which is cheaper, a Bib Gourmand or a Michelin-starred restaurant?
faq.a: A Bib Gourmand, by design: each country sets a price limit for a Bib meal. Starred restaurants have no limit; across the restaurants we track, a dinner tasting menu typically costs {{price1}} per person at one star.

faq.q: Is a Michelin Guide restaurant the same as a Michelin star restaurant?
faq.a: No. Being in the Michelin Guide means inspectors recommend the restaurant. Only a small share of the restaurants in the Guide hold stars.

Yes. It means anonymous Michelin inspectors judged the food to be high quality and great value. Many diners use the Bib list as their everyday guide and save starred restaurants for special occasions.
